headline: U.S. launches multi-domain strikes on Iran, blocks ports, seizes Strait of Hormuz
subheadline: U.S. Central Command struck Iranian air defenses, radars, missiles, and small boats using fighter jets, naval vessels, and one-way attack drones on 21 Tir.
lede: On 21 Tir, U.S. Central Command executed a multi‑domain strike wave against Iranian air‑defense systems, coastal radars, missile and drone capabilities, and small boats, employing fighter jets, naval vessels, and unmanned suicide vessels for the first time. Iran retaliated by launching at least four missiles from the Chamran base toward Bandar Abbas and the Konarak naval base, with explosions reported at 5:48, 5:51, 5:53, and 5:55. The U.S. Navy announced a comprehensive blockade of all Iranian ports effective 20:00 GMT and President Trump declared the U.S. would manage the Strait of Hormuz as ‘Guardian of Hormuz’ imposing a 20 % transit levy. Meanwhile, Houthi ballistic missile attacks on Saudi Arabia closed airports, and Israeli strikes killed weapons smuggler Mustafa Owaisi in Gaza and shelled Kfar Tibnit in Lebanon.

sections.title: Russian drone attacks hit Odesa, Stavropol, Chernigov
sections.body: Russian forces launched coordinated Geran‑4 kamikaze drone attacks on civilian vessels in the Odesa port’s Chornomorsk area, damaging a cargo ship, ferry, and fishing trawler. A subsequent drone strike hit the Mikhailovskaya oil depot in Stavropol, following an earlier attack on the Syzransky oil refinery. Three kamikaze drones struck an energy facility in Chernigov region, leaving the city without power, while Ukrainian troops fought near Ulanovo and Malaya Sloboda in Sumy and continued engagements in Ryzhevka, Pisarevka, and forest areas south of Ivolzhanskoye. French President Macron pledged SAMP‑T missile deliveries and granted production licenses for SCALP cruise missiles, Aster 30 missiles, and AASM Hammer bombs, and President Zelenskyy announced Ukraine’s FREYJA anti‑ballistic missile system development is now complete.

sections.title: U.S.-Iran escalation, Houthi strikes, Israeli actions
sections.body: U.S. Central Command struck Iranian air defenses, coastal radars, missile and drone capabilities, and small boats on 21 Tir using fighter jets, naval vessels, and unmanned suicide vessels for the first time. Iran responded by launching at least four missiles from the Chamran base toward Bandar Abbas and the Konarak naval base, with explosions recorded at 5:48, 5:51, 5:53, and 5:55. The U.S. Navy declared a comprehensive blockade of all Iranian ports effective 20:00 GMT and President Trump announced the U.S. would manage the Strait of Hormuz as ‘Guardian of Hormuz’ imposing a 20 % transit levy. Houthi forces fired ballistic missiles at Saudi Arabia, hitting Abha International Airport and prompting indefinite airport closures, while Israeli strikes killed weapons smuggler Mustafa Owaisi in Gaza and artillery shelled Kfar Tibnit in Lebanon, with IDF confirming deep‑strike explosions inside Lebanese territory.

sections.title: Intelligence Assessment
sections.body: The introduction of unmanned suicide vessels and a declared maritime blockade marks a new phase in the U.S.–Iran confrontation, raising miscalculation risks in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran’s missile strikes from Bandar Abbas demonstrate its willingness to retaliate despite U.S. superiority, while Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia open a second front that could involve Gulf states. Israel’s separate operations in Gaza and Lebanon, though currently distinct, could converge if Iranian proxies are activated, reflecting broader regional escalation.
